obligation: EAP notifications (project emergency)
trigger: Impending or actual sudden release of water (project emergency, 12.3(b)(9)), for example an uncontrolled gate opening with a surge downstream
deadline: Immediately, per the EAP notification flowchart
notify: Downstream residents by siren where installed; county emergency management; state and federal agencies listed in the EAP
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the event is or may become a project emergency
owner: HOC shift supervisor or plant operator (may act without waiting); Vice President, Dam Safety

obligation: Local law enforcement and county emergency management
citation: FERC Security Program Rev. 3A, sec. 4.2 and 7.4.1 (Internal Emergency Response)
trigger: Serious security incident at a project, including any unauthorized control of gates or units
deadline: Immediately, in parallel with local control and any EAP step
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - required by the Security Plans of Group 1 and 2 dams
owner: Vice President, Corporate Security (security dispatch makes the call)

obligation: Condition affecting safety of project works: initial report
trigger: Discovery of a security incident (physical and/or cyber) or of any misoperation of a gate or other facility that controls release of impounded water
deadline: As soon as practicable after the condition is discovered, preferably within 72 hours, without unduly interfering with emergency action
notify: FERC Regional Engineer by email or telephone

obligation: Condition affecting safety of project works: written report
trigger: After the initial report
deadline: Within the time the Regional Engineer specifies; verified under 12.13; causes, preceding events, measures taken, damage, injuries, private property damage

obligation: Deaths, serious injuries, or rescues at the project
trigger: Any death, serious injury, or rescue at project works or involving project operation (for example, from a surge caused by an unauthorized gate opening)
deadline: Initial report promptly after discovery; written report for project-related events (verified under 12.13)

obligation: Security incident or suspicious activity report to FERC
citation: FERC Security Program Rev. 3A, sec. 3.2 (bullet 11) and 4.2
trigger: Suspicious activity or a security incident at a project, unless law enforcement restricts reporting
deadline: As soon as practical (usually within one working day)
notify: FERC Regional Office (can be combined with the 12.10 initial report)

obligation: Suspicious activity report to the HSIN Dams portal
citation: FERC Security Program Rev. 3A, sec. 4.2; Appendix B
trigger: Suspicious activity or incident, regardless of apparent significance
deadline: No deadline stated; report promptly
notify: DHS Homeland Security Information Network suspicious activity tool
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary but recommended; the company has HSIN accounts

obligation: Other dam owners in the drainage basin
trigger: Security situation that could affect other dam owners (for example, releases or coordinated flows on the same river)
deadline: As quickly as possible
notify: Operators of upstream and downstream dams on the affected river system (9 agreements)

obligation: Temporary closure of recreation facilities for security
trigger: Closing recreation areas or project use for security reasons for 30 days or less
deadline: As soon as practical (usually within one working day); closures over 30 days need prior coordination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if recreation areas are closed

obligation: Reportable Cyber Security Incident: initial notification (medium impact)
trigger: Determination that a Cyber Security Incident compromised or disrupted a medium impact BES Cyber System (HOC-A or HOC-B), its ESP, or its EACMS; or an attempt to compromise
deadline: Within 1 hour after determining a Reportable Cyber Security Incident; by the end of the next calendar day after determining an attempt to compromise. Include functional impact, attack vector, and level of intrusion if known
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - medium impact BES Cyber Systems at the HOCs (C-DAMS-R03)

obligation: Reportable Cyber Security Incident: updates
trigger: New or changed information on functional impact, attack vector, or level of intrusion
deadline: Within 7 calendar days of determining the new or changed information

obligation: Reportable Cyber Security Incident: low impact assets
trigger: Determination that a Cyber Security Incident at an asset containing low impact BES Cyber Systems (for example PD-04) is a Reportable Cyber Security Incident
deadline: The standard sets no time; company procedure PRC-03.3 uses the CIP-008 timing: within 1 hour of the determination
notify: E-ISAC (unless prohibited by law); CISA voluntarily at the same time

obligation: NERC EOP-004-4 event report
trigger: An Attachment 1 event that applies to a GO or GOP (for example, damage or destruction of a Facility from actual or suspected intentional human action, or a physical threat to a Facility or BES control center)
deadline: By the later of 24 hours after recognizing the event met a threshold or the end of the next business day (4 p.m. local time)
notify: NERC and the parties in the Operating Plan (Reliability Coordinator, SERC, law enforcement where relevant); a DOE-417 form may be used instead when DOE-417 is also required
clock_starts: Recognition that the event met a threshold

obligation: DOE-417 Emergency Alert
citation: Form DOE-417 criteria 1-9; Federal Energy Administration Act sec. 13(b); OMB 1901-0288
trigger: Emergency Alert criteria, including a Reportable Cyber Security Incident or a cyber event that causes interruptions of electrical system operations
deadline: Within 1 hour after the incident
notify: DOE CESER (DOE-417 online system); sharing with NERC, the E-ISAC, and CISA can be selected on the form
applies_at_this_tier: To be confirmed - the company is not a Balancing Authority or Reliability Coordinator; filer role being confirmed with DOE and the Balancing Authorities (P03 G-227). Until then the NERC compliance team coordinates with the Balancing Authority on who files

obligation: DOE-417 Normal Report
trigger: Normal Report criteria, including a cyber event that could potentially impact electric power system adequacy or reliability, when no Emergency Alert criterion applies
deadline: Within 6 hours after the incident
applies_at_this_tier: To be confirmed - the company is not a Balancing Authority or Reliability Coordinator; filer role being confirmed with DOE and the Balancing Authorities (P03 G-227). Until then the NERC compliance team coordinates with the Balancing Authority on who files

obligation: DOE-417 Attempted Cyber Compromise
trigger: Attempted cyber compromise of a high or medium impact BES Cyber System or its EACMS, when no higher criterion applies
deadline: By the end of the next calendar day after the determination of the attempted cyber compromise
applies_at_this_tier: To be confirmed - the company is not a Balancing Authority or Reliability Coordinator; filer role being confirmed with DOE and the Balancing Authorities (P03 G-227). Until then the NERC compliance team coordinates with the Balancing Authority on who files

obligation: DOE-417 System Report
trigger: System Report criteria (for example, physical threats to a Facility or control center), when no higher criterion applies
deadline: By the later of 24 hours after recognition or the end of the next business day (4:00 p.m. local time)
applies_at_this_tier: To be confirmed - the company is not a Balancing Authority or Reliability Coordinator; filer role being confirmed with DOE and the Balancing Authorities (P03 G-227). Until then the NERC compliance team coordinates with the Balancing Authority on who files

obligation: DOE-417 final report
trigger: Every filed DOE-417 report
deadline: Final report within 72 hours
applies_at_this_tier: To be confirmed - the company is not a Balancing Authority or Reliability Coordinator; filer role being confirmed with DOE and the Balancing Authorities (P03 G-227). Until then the NERC compliance team coordinates with the Balancing Authority on who files

obligation: Balancing Authority and Transmission Operator notice of lost capability
citation: Generator interconnection and ancillary service agreements with the two Balancing Authorities (contract and operating procedure)
trigger: Units or Blackstart Resources unavailable, or HOC control lost
deadline: Immediately by voice on recorded lines; ICCP status updates as restored
notify: Balancing Authority and Transmission Operator control room for the affected area

obligation: SEC materiality determination
trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.5)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 filing
trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the Attorney General so determines; plausible for a dam-related public safety concern

obligation: SEC annual cybersecurity disclosure
trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents

obligation: State data breach notification (each state where affected individuals reside)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information (for example, employee records taken during an intrusion)
deadline: Varies by state; outside counsel keeps the state matrix
notify: Affected residents; state attorneys general or regulators and consumer reporting agencies where required
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information is involved; not expected for an OT-only intrusion

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (a 15-day extension on written good cause applies only to this notice)
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Only if personal information of Florida residents is involved
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (no good-cause extension for this notice)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent (for example, the payroll processor)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - vendors holding Florida residents' personal information

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any ransom payment is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA

obligation: Law enforcement and CISA report (voluntary)
citation: FERC Security Program Rev. 3A, sec. 9.4 (coordination with authorities such as the FBI); no statutory deadline
trigger: Suspected intrusion into control systems or extortion
deadline: As early as practical, the same day

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until it takes effect

obligation: SL-1 and SL-2 client notice
citation: Contract operations and monitoring service agreements (contract, not law)
trigger: Incident affecting the COC, the DSMS, or client data or plants
deadline: Per contract (24 hours for confirmed incidents affecting client systems or data)
owner: Vice President, Hydro Services; Vice President, Dam Safety Monitoring Services

obligation: Offtaker notice
citation: Power purchase and capacity agreements (contract, not law)
trigger: Event affecting scheduled energy or capacity
deadline: Per contract; schedule changes by phone at once
notify: Offtaker control centers and contract managers

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: 52.204-25(d): within 1 business day of identification; 52.204-23(c): within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
